statusMeanings.PASS: Every evidence slot the derivation rule requires is present and exists in this tree, and the row carries no evidenceGap. Says nothing about production fitness beyond what the cited evidence covers.
statusMeanings.PARTIAL: The mechanism exists and something in this tree gates it, but at least one required evidence slot is missing or a named gap remains. The gap is always named in evidenceGap.
statusMeanings.FAIL: A user-visible capability is known to be broken, or the evidence needed to claim it is absent while the defect it would have caught has already shipped. A FAIL row is a finding, not a placeholder.
statusMeanings.NOT_APPLICABLE: A decided, recorded exclusion with its reason. Never used for work that is merely unwritten.

derivation.method: Status is derived from what exists in this tree and what the gates actually assert, not from prose. A row is PASS only when every slot below is present AND exists AND evidenceGap is empty; anything else is PARTIAL with the missing slot named, unless a user-visible defect is known, in which case FAIL.
passRequires: oracleFixtures: at least one recording of pinned behaviour that the row's differential compares against
implementation: at least one Go file or package that carries the behaviour
tests: at least one named test that fails when the behaviour is wrong (existence checked, and the name must resolve to a real test function or harness file)
ci: at least one workflow job that runs that test
derivation.productionRule: AGENTS.md 22 and 29-30: a behaviour verified only against our own mock peer is `unverified` for production. Such rows cannot be PASS no matter how complete the fixture is, and the gap says so verbatim.
derivation.artifactRule: AGENTS.md 23 and 34: a release claim needs the shipped artifact, unpacked, started against a stock tree. Rows whose only evidence is the source tree carry that gap until a release-artifact result exists.
derivation.failRule: AGENTS.md 40: a defect that shipped is recorded here even after it is fixed, because the row's status is about the evidence layer that allowed it through. A fixed mechanism promotes a row from FAIL only when the gate that would have caught it exists and has run.

rows.area: Provider transport on the real internet (TLS, proxy, timeouts, decompression, redirects)

wouldGoRedIfWrong.explanation: An untrusted certificate must be refused with an error naming the TLS stage and the provider host and carrying no credential. The row previously had no gate at all for any network failure class; this test plus the DNS, connect and proxy siblings are that gate, and the artifact-level half is TestProviderTransportFailureIsCausalThroughTheShippedBinary.

evidenceGap: CLOSED 2026-10-29 -- THE INTERNET-SHAPED GATE. Every production-transport property was asserted against a recording peer that answers HTTP quickly and correctly, so the shapes a real network produces had no test. `internal/outbound/transport_internet_shape_test.go` now drives the PRODUCTION transport against a peer for each failure class, and each assertion is three-part: the error exists, it NAMES the stage and the provider host, and it does NOT contain the request's bearer token. TLS: an untrusted certificate is refused (`TestProductionTransportRefusesAnUntrustedCertificate`). DNS: the RFC 2606 `.invalid` TLD cannot resolve (`TestProductionTransportNamesADNSFailure`). Connect: a port that was just closed refuses (`TestProductionTransportNamesAConnectRefusal`). Proxy: a proxy answering 407 is named as the proxy, not as the provider (`TestProductionTransportNamesAProxyRefusal`). Timeout: a peer that accepts and never answers is attributed to the header stage (`TestProductionTransportAttributesATimeoutToTheHeaderStage`, pre-existing). The connect test's expected wording is deliberately platform-neutral ("connect" + "refused"), because Unix says `connect: connection refused` and Windows says `connectex: ... actively refused it`, and a host-specific phrase would have made the gate untransportable

CLOSED 2026-10-29 -- THROUGH THE SHIPPED ARTIFACT, which is what AGENTS.md 23 and 35 require. `tests/e2e`'s `TestProviderTransportFailureIsCausalThroughTheShippedBinary` boots the built binary, points a provider's chat URL at a local TLS peer whose certificate cannot chain, drives a real completion through `/api/backends/chat-completions/generate`, and asserts the JSON the browser receives carries `error` exactly as pinned's branch sends it PLUS a `message` that names the TLS stage and contains no credential -- and that the untrusted peer was never reached. THE TEETH WERE OBSERVED: removing the `message` member from `pinnedChatCompletionErrorFlagWithCause` turns it red with `the failure body carries no message, so the user sees no cause (this is the P0-A shape): {"error":true}` (exit 1); the byte copy was restored and the test went green

GoTavern diverges deliberately and declares it (`internal/server/chat_completions.go:141-154`): `error` stays exactly what pinned sends and a `message` member is added. The artifact test asserts BOTH halves -- the pinned member unchanged and the additive one present -- so the divergence cannot silently become a replacement

rows.area: Streaming SSE framing, incremental render and cancellation

wouldGoRedIfWrong.explanation: the row's claims about streaming sse framing, incremental render and cancellation rest on this test; deleting or weakening it makes the row unsupported, and the checker fails a row whose named test does not exist

rows.notes: Streaming has the deepest browser instrumentation in the tree (frame-by-frame render alignment on both legs). The network half has its own artefact (tests/browser/streaming-framing-comparison.json) with a real TCP hop behind it, and that artefact is now GREEN and gate-checked: browser-differential.yml run 40682654579 passed the comparator (step 16) with both subjects reporting the same partial text. THE CUT FIRES AT A BYTE OFFSET ON A FRAME BOUNDARY, not timed against the page: framesToBytes(3) = 513 of the peer's 2,565 bytes, so both subjects deliver and render content before the cut -- measured contentStates 2, textAfterCut "Hello from the", releasedBytes 349, plaintextOffsetAtCut 513, identically on both. The earlier reasoning is retained because it is WHY the cut point is a frame boundary: a cut INSIDE a record leaves both frontends before their error path with zero content states (measured, runs 40316734219, 40322630841, 40324760750), and a head-of-body cut delivers no body at all, so neither produces partial text to compare. The head-of-body vehicle this row previously cited as PROVEN (run 40331271988) is superseded and retired. Buffering-proxy mode is a DECIDED EXCLUSION, not a gap: a hop that releases the whole body in ONE write makes the number of rendered states a function of the browser commit schedule rather than of the server (measured 2 on GoTavern and 1 on pinned, run 40299346339), so that mode was deleted and its claim is NOT made. Status stays PARTIAL on the two surviving gaps below -- the TLS-close gap and the absent ordering gate -- not on inertia: the network half is proven, the row is not. RE-DERIVED 2026-10-29: the two remaining gaps are closed by committed tests (a graceful TLS shutdown mid-frame, and the frame-ORDER property for a complete and a cancelled stream), and the row's browser instrumentation was already green and gate-checked, so the row carries no evidence gap and is PASS rather than PARTIAL. The buffering-proxy mode stays a DECIDED EXCLUSION in this row's notes, which is a decision and not a gap. CLOSURE RECORD (kept out of evidenceGap because a PASS row may not carry gaps): CLOSED 2026-10-29 -- MID-STREAM TLS CLOSE. The row said the fault 'is a socket close on plain HTTP' and that a TLS fatal alert was not reproduced; the first half was STALE (TestProductionTransportSurfacesAMidStreamCloseCausally already starts a TLS server and hijacks the connection), and the second half is now covered in BOTH directions: an ABRUPT close (existing test) and a GRACEFUL TLS shutdown mid-frame, where the server hijacks its `*tls.Conn` and closes it properly so a close_notify goes out. `TestProductionTransportTreatsAGracefulTLSShutdownMidStreamAsTruncation` requires that case to reach the caller as an ERROR (a silent success would show half an answer as a complete one), that the bytes that DID arrive are still delivered, that the error is classifiable (unexpected EOF / truncation / closed / reset) and that it carries no credential. Teeth observed: returning `io.EOF` instead of the mid-stream error turns it red with 'a provider that shut the TLS session down mid-frame produced NO error' CLOSED 2026-10-29 -- THE ORDERING PROPERTY, ASSERTED AS A PROPERTY RATHER THAN AS A RECORDED PARTIAL TEXT. `TestProductionTransportPreservesProviderFrameOrder` makes a provider write 200 distinguishable SSE frames one per write, with a flush after each so they arrive in separate reads, then requires the received bytes to equal the sent bytes AND the parsed frame indices to be 0..199 in order with none dropped or duplicated. Teeth observed: `count = count/2` in the stream reader turns it red with 'the streamed bytes differ from what the provider wrote (sent 3290 bytes, received 1590, first difference at byte 7)'. `TestProductionTransportDeliversACancelledStreamAsAnOrderedPrefix` closes the CANCELLATION half of the same property: after a mid-stream cancel, the bytes the caller holds must be a PREFIX of what the provider wrote -- the beginning of the real answer, not a reshuffled fragment -- which is what makes a per-run 'partial text at the moment of abort' observation unnecessary for the ordering claim

Two gaps are real and remain: no gate asserts startup makes no non-essential network access, and the startup-differential fixtures still begin from fresh or migrated roots rather than a populated stock tree (a populated tree is covered by the longlived e2e leg and the packaged drop-in gate, not by a startup fixture). session.purpose: The whole-session differential AGENTS.md 34/38 asks for, inventoried against the harness that exists. It proves the claim above: every step has a probe, no probe shares a runtime with another, so there is no session.

steps.userAction: open the pinned frontend root in a browser
open a chat and see its history
send a message and receive a completion
send with streaming on, then cancel mid-stream
reload the page and see the conversation back
steps.notImplemented: no probe reads state back through the frontend after a reload; chats-save-get compares the HTTP round trip, not the browser's rehydration

canonicalisation.method: Each step's observation is compared after replacing those four classes with markers by FIELD PATH, never by regex over the whole document, and the replacement is recorded beside the observation so it cannot be silently widened. Byte equality is never claimed for a field that carries a clock.
